citations.quote:
This item fixes finite combinatorial vocabulary for outcome laws of a
two-station comparison. No physical interpretation, measurement model,
dynamics or locality assertion is made here; the physical readings are fixed
on the page of this pair. No choice principle is used.

**(a) Binary correlation model.** Let $I$ and $J$ be finite nonempty sets, the
**setting labels** of the two stations, and put
$\Sigma:=\{-1,+1\}$ for the common **outcome labels**. A **binary correlation
model** on $(I,J)$ is a family
$$\mu=(\mu_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J},\qquad \mu_{ij}:\Sigma\times\Sigma\to[0,1],$$
of functions with the normalization
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=1 \qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in I\times J$$
([[def-finite-sum]]). Each $\mu_{ij}$ is the **joint law** of the setting pair
$(i,j)$: it is the outcome-weight function of a finite probability space on
the four outcomes $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ in the sense of
[[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]], and sums over $\Sigma\times\Sigma$
are finite sums.

**(b) Marginals.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$ the **marginal law of the first
station** and the **marginal law of the second station** are
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon):=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma .$$

**(c) No-signalling.** The model $\mu$ is **no-signalling** when the marginal
law of the first station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}$ for all $i\in I$ and all $j,j'\in J$, and the
marginal law of the second station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $j\in J$ and all $i,i'\in I$. The word is
used as a name for this pair of identities about the tables; no spatial or
causal claim is attached to it.

**(d) Correlations and the CHSH functional.** Assume $I=J=\{0,1\}$. The
**correlation** of the setting pair $(i,j)$ and the **CHSH functional** of the
model are the real numbers
$$E_{ij}(\mu):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma} \varepsilon\,\delta\,\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad S(\mu):=E_{00}(\mu)+E_{01}(\mu)+E_{10}(\mu)-E_{11}(\mu).$$

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) introduce finite tables, their marginals, the
no-signalling identities and one linear functional of four correlations. They
assert no physical assumption, no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law
for a real apparatus and no statement about nature; the identification of a
laboratory arrangement with a model $\mu$ is a separate physical matter.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3, the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5 as inherited through the cited
spin-$s$ model and spin-spectrum result (only their internal-factor content
is used here), the
internal-factor assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6 and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), together with the
composite, observable and measurement readings of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]], the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared spin-half factors.** A **declared spin-half factor** is the
internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ of the spin-$s$ model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with spin label
$s=\tfrac12$, with its orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, the self-adjoint
matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) and the spin
observables $S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, explicitly assigned under P2 on $V$ as sharp observables with unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$, using the internal-factor assignment of P6 clause (ii). For a unit direction $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. Put $A_n:=n\cdot\sigma$. The Pauli identities of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) give
$A_n^*=A_n$ and $A_n^2=I$ for unit $n$. Each Pauli matrix has trace zero,
so $A_n$ has trace zero; its eigenvalues are $+1,-1$, each once. Thus
$S_n=(\hbar/2)A_n$ has eigenvalues $\pm\hbar/2$ with projections
$$P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,n\cdot\sigma\bigr), \qquad \varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\},$$
and the label $\varepsilon$ attached to the projection $P_{n,\varepsilon}$ is
the **sign label** of the outcome; the outcome coordinate is
$\varepsilon\hbar/2$, read in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, while the sign label
itself is dimensionless.

**(b) Declared arrangement.** A **declared spin correlation arrangement**
consists of: the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared
spin-half factors, with inclusion $\kappa$, in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] (a
declared pair of distinguishable subsystems whose assigned spaces are the two
internal factors); a **declared preparation** $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$,
the set of density operators on the composite
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); and two unit
**setting directions** $a_{0},a_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the first station and
$b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the second station. The setting labels are
$I=J=\{0,1\}$.

**(c) Declared local sign measurements.** For the first station and setting
$i\in I$, the **declared local sign measurement** is the declared ideal sharp
measurement whose outcome structure is the pair
$(P_{a_{i},+}\otimes I,\;P_{a_{i},-}\otimes I)$ with the sign labels $\pm1$:
these are the spectral projections of the local readout of the assigned
observable $(S_{a_{i}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ on the declared composite, the local
readout being constructed through the spectral measure by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] and
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]]. The second station's
declared local sign measurement for setting $j$ is
$(I\otimes P_{b_{j},+},\;I\otimes P_{b_{j},-})$, defined symmetrically.

**(d) Declared joint sign measurement and tables.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$
the **declared joint sign measurement** of the setting pair is the declared
ideal sharp measurement of the composite whose outcome structure is
$$E_{ij}:=\bigl(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}\bigr)_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma}, \qquad E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta},$$
with the pair of sign labels as its labels: by the identities $P_{n,\varepsilon}^*=P_{n,\varepsilon}$,
$P_{n,\varepsilon}^2=P_{n,\varepsilon}$,
$P_{n,+}P_{n,-}=0$ and $P_{n,+}+P_{n,-}=I$ from (a), each factor is an
orthogonal projection, and the tensor calculus of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] gives
$E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)E_{ij}(\varepsilon',\delta')=
\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}\delta_{\delta\delta'}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$
and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=I$, so this is a
finite family of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, as
required by clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Its
**outcome law** in the declared preparation $\rho$ is
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr), \qquad (\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma,$$
read from clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
(compare P2 clause (ii), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).
The **correlation table of the arrangement** is the family
$\nu^{\rho}=(\nu^{\rho}_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, which is a binary
correlation model on $(I,J)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a); its correlations
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$, its marginals and its CHSH functional $S(\nu^{\rho})$ are
the ones of clauses (b) and (d) of that definition, and are written
$S(\rho;a_{0},a_{1};b_{0},b_{1})$ when the arrangement data are displayed.

**(e) Declared local-response models of the arrangement.** A **declared
local-response model of the arrangement** is a local-response representation,
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]], of the
correlation table $\nu^{\rho}$. It is a model of the same four tables: it
consists of a probability space of **specifications** and of per-station
response laws, subject to the representation identity, and it need not be a
model of the framework's state space. The arrangement **admits a
local-response model** when such a representation exists.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix model vocabulary. They assign no spatial
position, worldline, spatial separation or temporal order to the two factors;
they assert no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus, no detection procedure
and no measured correlation; they do not assert that the composite is prepared
by any particular laboratory procedure. Whether a laboratory arrangement
realizes the declared preparation, the declared directions and the declared
sign measurements is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this
definition; the model's assignments of states to preparations and of spectral
projections to quantities are the readings of P1, P2 and P3 fixed on the
earlier pages.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis
of the tensor construction cited below. Let $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ carry the
orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and let
$$\sigma_{x}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{y}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_{z}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
be the Pauli matrices of clause (e) of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] in the ordered basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$; for $a=(a_{x},a_{y},a_{z})\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$\sigma_{a}:=a_{x}\sigma_{x}+a_{y}\sigma_{y}+a_{z}\sigma_{z}$, and for
$\varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$ put
$$P_{a,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,\sigma_{a}\bigr).$$
Let $V\widehat\otimes V$ be the completed tensor product with inclusion
$\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and let
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr)\in V\widehat\otimes V, \qquad q:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})+\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) for every unit $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $\varepsilon\in\Sigma$ the
operator $P_{a,\varepsilon}$ is an orthogonal projection on $V$,
$P_{a,+}+P_{a,-}=I$ and
$P_{a,\varepsilon}P_{a,\varepsilon'}=\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}P_{a,\varepsilon}$;

(b) $\|\Psi\|=1$ and the four vectors $\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),
\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-})$ are mutually orthogonal, so
$(\Psi,q,\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{+}),\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{-}))$ is an
orthonormal basis of $V\widehat\otimes V$;

(c) for all unit $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and all
$\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a\cdot b\bigr);$$

(d) the marginals of the four numbers in (c) are
$$\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle=\tfrac12 =\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle,$$
and their correlation is
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\varepsilon\,\delta\, \bigl\langle(P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =-a\cdot b .$$

The lemma is a finite-dimensional computation in the tensor product; it
asserts no preparation, measurement or physical interpretation. The Axiom of
Countable Choice enters only through the construction of the completed tensor
product cited from [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].

Adopt the declared spin correlation arrangement of
[[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: the composite
$V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared spin-half factors with orthonormal basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$, a declared preparation $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$, the
setting directions $a_{0},a_{1},b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and the four
declared joint sign measurements with outcome laws
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\bigr), \qquad P_{a,\varepsilon}=\tfrac12(I+\varepsilon\,a\cdot\sigma) .$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of
the cited suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), and
take the **singlet preparation**
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\Bigr), \qquad \rho_{\Psi}:=T_{\Psi,\Psi},$$
where $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is the rank-one operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Then:

(a) for every $(i,j)\in\{0,1\}^{2}$ and all $\varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma$,
$$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta) =\bigl\langle(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta})\Psi,\Psi\bigr\rangle =\tfrac14\bigl(1-\varepsilon\delta\,a_{i}\cdot b_{j}\bigr);$$

(b) the correlations of the arrangement are
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$ and
$$S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}) =-\bigl[a_{0}\cdot b_{0}+a_{0}\cdot b_{1}+a_{1}\cdot b_{0}-a_{1}\cdot b_{1}\bigr] =-\,(a_{0}\cdot(b_{0}+b_{1})+a_{1}\cdot(b_{0}-b_{1}));$$
in particular, for the unit directions
$a_{0}=(0,0,1)$, $a_{1}=(1,0,0)$, $b_{0}=(1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ and
$b_{1}=(-1,0,1)/\sqrt2$ one has $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$, so
$\bigl|S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})\bigr|=2\sqrt2>2$;

(c) consequently the correlation table $\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}}$ of the arrangement
at those directions admits no local-response model in the sense of clause (e)
of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]]: there is no local-response
representation of the four tables
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]) with these laws;

(d) the marginal sign laws of the arrangement are
$\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\tfrac12=
\nu^{\rho_{\Psi},B}_{ij}(\delta)$ for every setting pair and every direction, so
the table is no-signalling in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]]; and a discarded declared local
instrument on either factor leaves the reduced preparation of the other factor
and every local outcome law of that factor unchanged
([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).

The item is a conditional model computation: it asserts no measured
correlation, no apparatus and no empirical fact, and its exclusion is exactly
of the declared local-response class of these four tables. Higher singleton
claims about hidden variables in general are not asserted.

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited
spectral-law supplier. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$
be a unit vector, $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ the associated pure preparation, and
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$ its
reduced preparations. Then:

**(a) Product preparations factorize.** If $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$, then for every bounded effect $F$ on $H$ and every bounded
effect $F'$ on $K$
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(F\otimes F')\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}F)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F').$$
In particular, for a declared finite-outcome measurement of $A$ with effect
family $(F_{i})$ and one of $B$ with $(F'_{j})$, the joint outcome
probabilities factorize, $p(i,j)=p_{A}(i)p_{B}(j)$: in a product preparation
the two subsystems have independent local statistics.

**(b) Non-product pure preparations are correlated.** If $\Psi$ is not a
product vector and
$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is its Schmidt expansion
with $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, then the rank-one effects
$P:=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$ on $H$ and $P':=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ on $K$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P\otimes P')\bigr)=0\ \ne\ s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P'),$$
so the joint law of the corresponding two-outcome local measurements does not
factorize; the product of the marginal probabilities exceeds the joint
probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$.

**(c) Scope.** The statement is a conditional computation for pure
preparations of the declared composite; it asserts no dynamics, no
interaction, no apparatus realization, no measured correlation and no
empirical fact, and it does not claim that a joint law failing to factorize
establishes any particular physical mechanism.

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}=0$ when two of $i,j,k$ coincide, and otherwise $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$; the sum ranges over $k\in\{x,y,z\}$. The same convention with indices $1,2,3$ uses the order-preserving relabelling $(1,2,3)=(x,y,z)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); write $T_{x,z}x'=\langle x',z\rangle x$ for rank-one operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]) and $\operatorname{tr}$ for the trace of a trace-class operator ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(a) There is a unique linear map $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(H\widehat\otimes K)\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_KT)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(A\otimes I_K)\bigr)$$

for every trace-class $T$ and every $A\in\mathcal B(H)$; it satisfies $\|\operatorname{Tr}_KT\|_1\le\|T\|_1$ and is independent of any chosen orthonormal basis of $K$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ maps self-adjoint positive trace-class operators to self-adjoint positive trace-class operators (positivity in the bounded-operator sense of [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), is trace preserving ($\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_KT=\operatorname{tr}T$), and maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

(c) On rank-one operators, $\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle_K\,T_{u,u'}$.

The analogous map $\operatorname{Tr}_H$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_HT)A)=\operatorname{tr}(T(I_H\otimes A))$ for $A\in\mathcal B(K)$. No claim is made about instruments or conditioning.

Let $\mu$ be a binary correlation model on the setting sets $I=J=\{0,1\}$
with outcome labels $\Sigma=\{-1,+1\}$, with correlations $E_{ij}(\mu)$ and
CHSH functional $S(\mu)$ as in
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clauses (d), and suppose that
$\mu$ admits a local-response representation with response laws
$(\alpha_{i})_{i\in I}$, $(\beta_{j})_{j\in J}$ on a probability space
$(\Lambda,\Sigma_{\Lambda},\mathbb P)$
([[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]]). Then
$$\bigl|S(\mu)\bigr|\le 2 .$$
The statement is a theorem about the tables and their representation; it
asserts no measurement, no dynamics, no spatial or causal structure, and it
contains no physics. No choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: [Directions and singlet values] The four directions are unit vectors with $a_{0}\cdot b_{0}=a_{0}\cdot b_{1}=a_{1}\cdot b_{0}=1/\sqrt2$ and $a_{1}\cdot b_{1}=-1/\sqrt2$. By [L1] and [L2], $E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-a_{i}\cdot b_{j}$, so $E_{00}=E_{01}=E_{10}=-1/\sqrt2$, $E_{11}=+1/\sqrt2$ and $S(\nu^{\rho_{\Psi}})=-2\sqrt2$; this is (a).

[Product-state tables] Write $u_{+}:=e_{+}$, $u_{-}:=e_{-}$. By [L3], for the product preparation $T_{u_{\tau}\otimes u_{-\tau},u_{\tau}\otimes u_{-\tau}}$ (with $\tau=+$ or $-$) the joint sign law at $(i,j)$ is $\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon\tau(a_{i})_{3})\cdot\tfrac12(1-\delta\tau(b_{j})_{3})$.

[Mixture tables] By [L1] the outcome law of a convex mixture is the corresponding convex combination of the laws, so the two product tables of step 1.2 average to $\nu^{M}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=\tfrac14\bigl[\tfrac12(1+\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})(1-\delta(b_{j})_{3})+\tfrac12(1-\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})(1+\delta(b_{j})_{3})\bigr]=\tfrac14(1-\varepsilon\delta(a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3})$; this is the table formula of (b).

[Mixture correlations and CHSH value] Summing the table of step 2.1 with the product signs gives $E_{ij}(\nu^{M})=-(a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3}$; substituting $(a_{0})_{3}=1$, $(a_{1})_{3}=0$, $(b_{0})_{3}=(b_{1})_{3}=1/\sqrt2$ gives $E_{00}=E_{01}=-1/\sqrt2$ and $E_{10}=E_{11}=0$, hence $S(\nu^{M})=-1/\sqrt2-1/\sqrt2-0+0=-\sqrt2$; this completes (b).

[Explicit representation] Choose a two-point specification space $\Lambda=\{1,2\}$ with weights $\mathbb P(\{1\})=\mathbb P(\{2\})=	frac12$ and define the response laws by the display of (c). Then for each $(i,j,\varepsilon,\delta)$ one has $\int_{\Lambda}\alpha_{i}(\lambda,\varepsilon) eta_{j}(\lambda,\delta)\,d\mathbb P(\lambda)=	frac12\cdot	frac12(1+\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})\cdot	frac12(1-\delta(b_{j})_{3})+	frac12\cdot	frac12(1-\varepsilon(a_{i})_{3})\cdot	frac12(1+\delta(b_{j})_{3})=	frac14 igl(1-\varepsilon\delta(a_{i})_{3}(b_{j})_{3} igr)=
u^{M}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ by step 2.1, so $(\alpha, eta,\mathbb P)$ is a local-response representation of $
u^{M}$; the bound $|S(
u^{M})|\le2$ then follows from [L5] and is consistent with the value $-\sqrt2$ of (b), since $\sqrt2\le2$. This is (c).

[Common marginals and comparison] Summing the mixture table of step 2.1 over the distant label gives $\tfrac12$ for each local label, and the singlet's marginals are $\tfrac12$ by [L2]; the reduced preparations are $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\tfrac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}=\tfrac12I$ and, expanding $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ in the product basis and applying [L4] linearly, $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho_{\Psi}=\tfrac12(T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+T_{e_{-},e_{-}})=\tfrac12I$, so both arrangements share every single-station statistic while their CHSH functionals are $2\sqrt2$ and $\sqrt2$ in absolute value. This is (d).

[Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 3.2 and 4.1 prove (a)-(d); only the declared arrangements, the singlet pairings, the product-factorization theorem, the spin-half outcome laws, the partial trace and the CHSH bound for representable models were used, and no measured correlation is asserted.

[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] and the
units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared spin-half factors.** A **declared spin-half factor** is the
internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ of the spin-$s$ model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with spin label
$s=\tfrac12$, with its orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, the self-adjoint
matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) and the spin
observables $S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$, explicitly assigned under P2 on $V$ as sharp observables with unit
$\mathrm{J\,s}$, using the internal-factor assignment of P6 clause (ii). For a unit direction $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$ put
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$. Put $A_n:=n\cdot\sigma$. The Pauli identities of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) give
$A_n^*=A_n$ and $A_n^2=I$ for unit $n$. Each Pauli matrix has trace zero,
so $A_n$ has trace zero; its eigenvalues are $+1,-1$, each once. Thus
$S_n=(\hbar/2)A_n$ has eigenvalues $\pm\hbar/2$ with projections
$$P_{n,\varepsilon}:=\tfrac12\bigl(I+\varepsilon\,n\cdot\sigma\bigr), \qquad \varepsilon\in\Sigma=\{-1,+1\},$$
and the label $\varepsilon$ attached to the projection $P_{n,\varepsilon}$ is
the **sign label** of the outcome; the outcome coordinate is
$\varepsilon\hbar/2$, read in the unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, while the sign label
itself is dimensionless.

**(b) Declared arrangement.** A **declared spin correlation arrangement**
consists of: the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ of two declared
spin-half factors, with inclusion $\kappa$, in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] (a
declared pair of distinguishable subsystems whose assigned spaces are the two
internal factors); a **declared preparation** $\rho\in D(V\widehat\otimes V)$,
the set of density operators on the composite
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]); and two unit
**setting directions** $a_{0},a_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the first station and
$b_{0},b_{1}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ for the second station. The setting labels are
$I=J=\{0,1\}$.

**(c) Declared local sign measurements.** For the first station and setting
$i\in I$, the **declared local sign measurement** is the declared ideal sharp
measurement whose outcome structure is the pair
$(P_{a_{i},+}\otimes I,\;P_{a_{i},-}\otimes I)$ with the sign labels $\pm1$:
these are the spectral projections of the local readout of the assigned
observable $(S_{a_{i}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ on the declared composite, the local
readout being constructed through the spectral measure by clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] and
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]]. The second station's
declared local sign measurement for setting $j$ is
$(I\otimes P_{b_{j},+},\;I\otimes P_{b_{j},-})$, defined symmetrically.

**(d) Declared joint sign measurement and tables.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$
the **declared joint sign measurement** of the setting pair is the declared
ideal sharp measurement of the composite whose outcome structure is
$$E_{ij}:=\bigl(P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta}\bigr)_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma}, \qquad E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=P_{a_{i},\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b_{j},\delta},$$
with the pair of sign labels as its labels: by the identities $P_{n,\varepsilon}^*=P_{n,\varepsilon}$,
$P_{n,\varepsilon}^2=P_{n,\varepsilon}$,
$P_{n,+}P_{n,-}=0$ and $P_{n,+}+P_{n,-}=I$ from (a), each factor is an
orthogonal projection, and the tensor calculus of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] gives
$E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)E_{ij}(\varepsilon',\delta')=
\delta_{\varepsilon\varepsilon'}\delta_{\delta\delta'}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$
and $\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=I$, so this is a
finite family of mutually orthogonal projections resolving the identity, as
required by clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Its
**outcome law** in the declared preparation $\rho$ is
$$\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr), \qquad (\varepsilon,\delta)\in\Sigma\times\Sigma,$$
read from clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
(compare P2 clause (ii), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).
The **correlation table of the arrangement** is the family
$\nu^{\rho}=(\nu^{\rho}_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$, which is a binary
correlation model on $(I,J)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-bell-binary-correlation-models]] clause (a); its correlations
$E_{ij}(\nu^{\rho})$, its marginals and its CHSH functional $S(\nu^{\rho})$ are
the ones of clauses (b) and (d) of that definition, and are written
$S(\rho;a_{0},a_{1};b_{0},b_{1})$ when the arrangement data are displayed.

**(e) Declared local-response models of the arrangement.** A **declared
local-response model of the arrangement** is a local-response representation,
in the sense of [[def-nrqm-bell-local-response-representation]], of the
correlation table $\nu^{\rho}$. It is a model of the same four tables: it
consists of a probability space of **specifications** and of per-station
response laws, subject to the representation identity, and it need not be a
model of the framework's state space. The arrangement **admits a
local-response model** when such a representation exists.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix model vocabulary. They assign no spatial
position, worldline, spatial separation or temporal order to the two factors;
they assert no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus, no detection procedure
and no measured correlation; they do not assert that the composite is prepared
by any particular laboratory procedure. Whether a laboratory arrangement
realizes the declared preparation, the declared directions and the declared
sign measurements is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this
definition; the model's assignments of states to preparations and of spectral
projections to quantities are the readings of P1, P2 and P3 fixed on the
earlier pages.

This item fixes finite combinatorial vocabulary for outcome laws of a
two-station comparison. No physical interpretation, measurement model,
dynamics or locality assertion is made here; the physical readings are fixed
on the page of this pair. No choice principle is used.

**(a) Binary correlation model.** Let $I$ and $J$ be finite nonempty sets, the
**setting labels** of the two stations, and put
$\Sigma:=\{-1,+1\}$ for the common **outcome labels**. A **binary correlation
model** on $(I,J)$ is a family
$$\mu=(\mu_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J},\qquad \mu_{ij}:\Sigma\times\Sigma\to[0,1],$$
of functions with the normalization
$$\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=1 \qquad\text{for every }(i,j)\in I\times J$$
([[def-finite-sum]]). Each $\mu_{ij}$ is the **joint law** of the setting pair
$(i,j)$: it is the outcome-weight function of a finite probability space on
the four outcomes $\Sigma\times\Sigma$ in the sense of
[[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]], and sums over $\Sigma\times\Sigma$
are finite sums.

**(b) Marginals.** For $(i,j)\in I\times J$ the **marginal law of the first
station** and the **marginal law of the second station** are
$$\mu^{A}_{ij}(\varepsilon):=\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \mu^{B}_{ij}(\delta):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad \varepsilon,\delta\in\Sigma .$$

**(c) No-signalling.** The model $\mu$ is **no-signalling** when the marginal
law of the first station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{A}_{ij}=\mu^{A}_{ij'}$ for all $i\in I$ and all $j,j'\in J$, and the
marginal law of the second station does not depend on the distant setting,
$\mu^{B}_{ij}=\mu^{B}_{i'j}$ for all $j\in J$ and all $i,i'\in I$. The word is
used as a name for this pair of identities about the tables; no spatial or
causal claim is attached to it.

**(d) Correlations and the CHSH functional.** Assume $I=J=\{0,1\}$. The
**correlation** of the setting pair $(i,j)$ and the **CHSH functional** of the
model are the real numbers
$$E_{ij}(\mu):=\sum_{\varepsilon\in\Sigma}\sum_{\delta\in\Sigma} \varepsilon\,\delta\,\mu_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta), \qquad S(\mu):=E_{00}(\mu)+E_{01}(\mu)+E_{10}(\mu)-E_{11}(\mu).$$

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) introduce finite tables, their marginals, the
no-signalling identities and one linear functional of four correlations. They
assert no physical assumption, no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law
for a real apparatus and no statement about nature; the identification of a
laboratory arrangement with a model $\mu$ is a separate physical matter.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following discipline for comparing the model with recorded data.

**(i) Declared model of each comparison.** A comparison of a model prediction with an experiment of the framework requires, in addition to the state and dynamics assumptions P1-P5, the following declared items: a **preparation model**, that is, a specification of the state or preparation assigned to the system together with the physical procedure that realizes it; an **isolation model**, that is, the energy operator used and a statement of the interactions neglected in the approximation; a **detection model**, that is, the response of the apparatus, including efficiency, resolution, background and any binning; and **sampling assumptions**, that is, the statistical model under which repetitions of the preparation and detection are combined. None of these items is supplied by the mathematical framework alone.

**(ii) Repetitions.** The treatment of repeated trials as independent and identically distributed draws from the model's outcome law is an additional statistical model of the apparatus and the procedure. It is not a consequence of the state postulate and is not guaranteed by the mathematics; where it is assumed it is stated, and where it fails (correlated trials, drifting preparation, dead time, selection) the statistical analysis must model the departure or record the limitation.

**(iii) Identification with uncertainty.** The claim "this apparatus realizes the preparation $\rho$ and the dynamics $H_{\mathrm{op}}$" and the claim "this detector realizes the effect $F$" are physical identifications: they are tested against recorded behaviour of the apparatus, carry uncertainty and can fail. They are not derived from the framework, and a model prediction obtained under them inherits their qualifications. Calibration procedures, control experiments and their limitations are recorded with the comparison.

**(iv) Empirical premises.** Where a measured value enters a deduction - a mass, a charge, a field strength, a detector efficiency - it enters as a qualified empirical premise with its uncertainty, conditions of measurement and source, and the conclusion of the deduction carries those qualifications. A deduction that uses a measured input is not an exact statement about nature.

**(v) Status.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted as the framework's conditions for comparing model with data. They make no claim that the framework or the apparatus description is exact; agreement of a prediction with a dataset is evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework and not a statement about nature deduced from the mathematics.

A finite family of finite-valued random variables $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ is **mutually independent** when for every nonempty $J\subseteq I$ and every selection $x_j\in X_j(\Omega)$,
$$\mathbb P(X_j=x_j\text{ for every }j\in J)=\prod_{j\in J}\mathbb P(X_j=x_j).$$
It is **pairwise independent** when this identity is required only for two distinct indices. The empty family is mutually independent vacuously, and a one-member family is mutually independent.

No choice principle is used. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space ([[def-probability-measure]]).

(a) _CHSH bound._ Let $A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ be random variables with values in $\{-1,1\}$ ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]]). Then the four expectations exist and

$$\bigl|\mathbb E[A_0B_0]+\mathbb E[A_0B_1]+\mathbb E[A_1B_0]-\mathbb E[A_1B_1]\bigr|\le2 .$$

(b) _Positive-probability sequences._ Let $N\ge1$, $m\ge1$, $p_1,\dots,p_m\ge0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^mp_j=1$, and let $X_1,\dots,X_N:\Omega\to\{1,\dots,m\}$ be mutually independent with $\mathbb P(X_k=j)=p_j$ for all $k,j$ ([[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]). Then for every sequence $(j_1,\dots,j_N)\in\{1,\dots,m\}^N$ with $p_{j_k}>0$ for every $k$,

$$\mathbb P\bigl(X_k=j_k\text{ for every }k\bigr)=\prod_{k=1}^Np_{j_k}>0 .$$

Consequently every event disjoint from this outcome has probability at most $1-\prod_kp_{j_k}<1$: any criterion that rejects at least one such sequence has positive failure probability under this sampling model.

(c) _Binomial frequency._ Let $S$ be binomial$(N,p)$ with $N\ge1$ and $p\in[0,1]$ ([[def-bernoulli-and-binomial-random-variables]]). Then the frequency $S/N$ satisfies $\mathbb E[S/N]=p$, $\operatorname{Var}(S/N)=p(1-p)/N$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$

$$\mathbb P\bigl(|S/N-p|\ge\varepsilon\bigr)\le\frac{p(1-p)}{N\varepsilon^2}.$$

(d) _Multinomial count law._ The number of sequences $(j_1,\dots,j_N)$ with prescribed fibre sizes $n_j:=\#\{k:j_k=j\}$ is the multinomial coefficient $\binom{N}{n_1,\dots,n_m}$ ([[def-multinomial-coefficient]]), and each such sequence has probability $\prod_{j=1}^mp_j^{n_j}$; in this displayed product use the zero-count convention $p^0:=1$ for every $p\in[0,1]$, including $p=0$. Hence the probability that the count vector equals $(n_1,\dots,n_m)$ is $\binom{N}{n_1,\dots,n_m}\prod_jp_j^{n_j}$.

No statistical inference, empirical claim or measured frequency is asserted; the lemma only computes probabilities of an explicitly specified independent sampling model.

Let $X,Y$ be integrable real or complex random variables on one probability
space.

1. For scalars $a,b$,
   $$\mathbb E[aX+bY]=a\,\mathbb E[X]+b\,\mathbb E[Y].$$
2. If $X$ and $Y$ are real-valued and $X\le Y$ almost surely, then
   $$\mathbb E[X]\le\mathbb E[Y].$$
3. $$|\mathbb E[X]|\le\mathbb E[|X|].$$

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space.

- If $X:\Omega\to[0,+\infty]$ is measurable, its **expectation** is the
  extended-valued integral
  $$\mathbb E[X]:=\int_\Omega X\,d\mathbb P\in[0,+\infty].$$
- If $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ or $X:\Omega\to\mathbb C$ is integrable in the sense
  of [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]], its
  **expectation** is again
  $$\mathbb E[X]:=\int_\Omega X\,d\mathbb P,$$
  now a finite real or complex number.

For an integrable real random variable,
$$\mathbb E[X]=\mathbb E[X^+]-\mathbb E[X^-],$$
where $X^+$ and $X^-$ are its positive and negative parts.

Throughout this page $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]), in particular an ordered field
([[def-ordered-field]]) and a field ([[def-field]]), and $\mathbb{N}$ is the set
of natural numbers ([[def-natural-numbers]]) with successor $\sigma(n) = n + 1$
([[def-nat-addition]]).

Let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a sequence of reals, written $a_k$ for
$a(k)$. **Finite sums and finite products of $a$ are defined by recursion on the
upper index**, which is legitimate because of the recursion theorem
([[thm-recursion]]). That theorem produces a function of one variable, so the
running index has to be carried along inside the value: applying it to the set
$A = \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{R}$, the starting element $(0, 0)$ and the function
$f(n, s) = (\sigma(n),\, s + a_n)$ gives a unique
$g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{R}$ with

$$g(0) = (0, 0), \qquad g(\sigma(n)) = f(g(n)) \quad (n \in \mathbb{N}).$$

Write $g(n) = \big(\pi_1(g(n)),\, \Sigma_n\big)$ for its two coordinates.

**The first coordinate is the index itself, and that is a small induction, not an
observation** ([[thm-induction-principle]]). Indeed $\pi_1(g(0)) = 0$; and if
$\pi_1(g(n)) = n$, then
$g(\sigma(n)) = f\big(\pi_1(g(n)), \Sigma_n\big) = \big(\sigma(\pi_1(g(n))),\, \Sigma_n + a_{\pi_1(g(n))}\big) = \big(\sigma(n),\, \Sigma_n + a_n\big)$,
so $\pi_1(g(\sigma(n))) = \sigma(n)$. By induction $\pi_1(g(n)) = n$ for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$. Only now may the second coordinate of the two displayed
clauses be read off, and doing so gives

$$\Sigma_0 = 0, \qquad \Sigma_{\sigma(n)} = \Sigma_n + a_n .$$

$\Sigma$ is moreover the **unique** function $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with those
two properties: if $\Sigma'$ also has them then $n \mapsto (n, \Sigma'_n)$ satisfies
the two clauses defining $g$, hence equals $g$ by the uniqueness clause of
[[thm-recursion]], so $\Sigma' = \Sigma$.

We write $\sum_{k < n} a_k := \Sigma_n$. The same construction with starting
element $(0, 1)$ and $f(n, p) = (\sigma(n),\, p \cdot a_n)$, with the same
induction on the first coordinate and the same uniqueness argument, gives the
unique $\Pi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with

$$\Pi_0 = 1, \qquad \Pi_{\sigma(n)} = \Pi_n \cdot a_n ,$$

and we write $\prod_{k < n} a_k := \Pi_n$.

**Notation.** For $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$ we abbreviate

$$\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k := \sum_{k < n+1} a_k, \qquad \prod_{k=0}^{n} a_k := \prod_{k < n+1} a_k,$$

and, for a general lower index $m$ with $m \le n + 1$, writing $d = n + 1 - m$
for the number of terms,

$$\sum_{k=m}^{n} a_k := \sum_{j < d} a_{m+j}, \qquad \prod_{k=m}^{n} a_k := \prod_{j < d} a_{m+j} .$$

When $m = n + 1$ we have $d = 0$ and the sum is **empty**, with value $0$, while
the empty product has value $1$. In the same spirit $\sum_{k=0}^{-1} a_k$ is
notation for the empty sum $\Sigma_0 = 0$ and $\prod_{k=0}^{-1} a_k$ for the
empty product $\Pi_0 = 1$; the index $-1$ never occurs as an element of
$\mathbb{N}$ and is only a way of writing "no terms".

Only finitely many values of $a$ enter $\sum_{k<n} a_k$, so the notation
$\sum_{k<n} a_k$ and $\prod_{k<n} a_k$ is also used for a list
$a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ of reals given without reference to any extension of the
list to all of $\mathbb{N}$: extend the list by $a_k = 0$ (respectively
$a_k = 1$) for $k \ge n$ and apply the definition above.

Let $X$ be a real random variable on a probability space.

- For $p>0$, the **$p$th absolute moment** of $X$ exists when $|X|^p$ is
  integrable, and is then
  $$\mathbb E[|X|^p].$$
- If $X$ is integrable, its **mean** is $\mathbb E[X]$.
- If $X$ is square-integrable, its **variance** is
  $$\operatorname{Var}(X):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])^2].$$

If $X$ and $Y$ are square-integrable real random variables on the same
probability space, their **covariance** is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y):=\mathbb E[(X-\mathbb E[X])(Y-\mathbb E[Y])].$$

If $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ is a finite pairwise-independent family, then
$$\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\sum_{i\in I}X_i\right)=\sum_{i\in I}\operatorname{Var}(X_i).$$
Pairwise independence, rather than mutual independence, is sufficient.

If $X$ is a square-integrable real random variable and $a>0$, then
$$\mathbb P(|X-\mathbb E[X]|\ge a)\le\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{a^2}.$$

derivations.claim: [Mean and variance of one sample correlation] Fix $(i,j)$ and put $X_{k}:=\Sigma_{ijk}\mathrm T_{ijk}$ for $k=1,\dots,n$. Each $X_{k}$ takes values in $\{-1,+1\}$, so $\mathbb E[X_{k}]=\sum_{\varepsilon,\delta}\varepsilon\delta\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)=E_{ij}$ by [F1] and [F3], and $X_{k}^{2}=1$ identically, so $\operatorname{Var}(X_{k})=\mathbb E[X_{k}^{2}]-\mathbb E[X_{k}]^{2}=1-E_{ij}^{2}\le1$ by [F4]; the $X_{k}$ are mutually independent because the corresponding pairs are, and $\widehat E_{ij}=\frac1n\sum_{k}X_{k}$. Hence $\mathbb E[\widehat E_{ij}]=\frac1n\sum_{k}\mathbb E[X_{k}]=E_{ij}$ by [F3], and $\operatorname{Var}(\widehat E_{ij})=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\operatorname{Var}(\sum_{k}X_{k})=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\sum_{k}\operatorname{Var}(X_{k})\le\frac{n}{n^{2}}=\frac1n$ by [F4]; this is (a).

[Positive failure probability] Let $(x_{ijk})$ be a sequence of outcomes with $p:=\prod_{i,j,k}
u^{ho}_{ij}(x_{ijk})>0$. By mutual independence [F2] the event that the sample equals this sequence has probability exactly $p>0$; if the criterion $C$ rejects this sequence, that is $(x_{ijk})
otin C$, then the singleton event $\{(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})=(x_{ijk})\}$ is contained in the failure event $\{(\Sigma_{ijk},\mathrm T_{ijk})
otin C\}$, so the failure probability is at least $p>0$.

[CHSH estimator moments and concentration] The four families $\{X_{k}\}_{k}$ for the four setting pairs involve disjoint groups of the $4n$ mutually independent random elements, so the four estimators $\widehat E_{ij}$ are mutually independent; by [F3] and [F4], $\mathbb E[\widehat S]=E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}=S$ and $\operatorname{Var}(\widehat S)=\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Var}(\widehat E_{ij})\le4\cdot\frac1n=\frac4n$ by step 1.1.
